prompt: In electron-impact (EI) MS, the molecular ion (M⁺•) is formed by:

options.label: Ejection of ONE electron by a 70-eV electron beam (giving a radical cation)
Protonation by a chemical reagent gas (giving [M+H]⁺)
Direct fragmentation of the molecule into charged pieces by the electron beam
Ejection of TWO electrons, forming a stable dication (M²⁺)

explanation: A 70-eV electron collides with the molecule and knocks out ONE valence electron, giving an odd-electron radical cation M⁺•. (Protonation [M+H]⁺ is chemical ionization CI, not EI. Dications are rare.) The radical cation then fragments to give the characteristic spectrum.
